client_brief:
Season four is finished and we would like something small to point people at it. Not a narrated trailer, and not three separate quote clips.

The three recordings in the pack are picture only. There is no sound on any of them, so please do not caption speech that is not there, and do not credit a line to a guest who is not shown saying it. Everything the viewer reads is text you set on screen, which is how the show already plays in a muted feed. A cleared instrumental bed is in the pack as daydrift_bed.wav.

Scope

Season four trailer: one named export, upright, twelve to fifteen seconds, music only. It moves through the three recorded episodes and names each one by its published title and its guest. At least three different shots, please, and no looping one recording to fill the time.

Season four trailer square cutdown: one named export, square, eight to ten seconds, music only, cut from the same material and finishing on a card that holds.

Episode covers: three named exports, square stills, one for episode two, one for episode five and one for episode eight. Each carries its published episode title, its guest and the sponsor line in full.

Titles, guest names and dates come from the season file and the show notes, spelled the way we publish them. The sponsor line is not ours to shorten, so it appears complete on every cover. The show name only survives as the artwork on the microphone flag, so take it from there rather than setting it in a typeface.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, a still montage PDF or an editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film, and no film in this pack carries speech.

Live action edits require adequate distinct footage. Looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent long form interview podcast with a YouTube channel, one guest per episode, made and recorded in the show's own room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A two person show: two hosts, one room, nine episodes a season.
brand_identity.about: DAYDRIFT is a slow, unhurried interview show built around one guest and one real conversation that runs the better part of an hour. It is made by two people in a room they know well, funded by a small paying membership and one renewing sponsor. The promise is intimacy: you are sitting in on a talk between people who like each other, not watching a broadcast.
brand_identity.audience: Regular listeners aged thirty to fifty, most of them listening at work through the day. About two hundred paying members at eight dollars a month, plus a few thousand free listeners who click through to the channel page.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Membership at eight dollars a month with one modest renewing sponsor. Squarely independent: above hobby, well below a network production. The look must read considered and hand made, never broadcast and never scrappy meme.
brand_identity.typography: Lyon Text (humanist serif), Regular, sets episode titles and cover topics: 64 px on the 1080 by 1350 covers, 78 px leading, and 72 px on the trailers. Cronos Pro Light (humanist sans) sets guest credits at 34 px and dates and the sponsor line at 26 px. The show name stays the hand drawn lettering from the mic flag, Foam Cream (#EDE4D3) on Deep Room Brown (#3A2E26). Never typeset the show name, and never set a cover topic in a sans.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and a little understated, the way two friends actually talk. We never oversell a guest. Example line the brand would write: "Episode eight. We sat down with her for an hour and did not want it to end."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files left. The show name only survives as artwork on the foam flag on the microphone, drawn years ago by a friend who has since moved away and left no source file. Last season's printed episode card exists only as the print file the printer returned. Everything else has to be rebuilt from those.
brand_identity.values: Honesty and warmth over polish. The show would rather be small and real than slick, and it wants a look it can keep running itself next season without re commissioning.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
